About HOTmate

Version 2.25.0 (1)

B737 · high-speed aerodynamic LOUT · predominantly aluminum surfaces · flaps/slats retracted.

For verification of your own calculations. Follow company procedures and the applicable approved documentation.

Dataset & sources

Installed season: Winter 2025–2026.

HOT, snowfall intensity, application limits and relevant notes: CWOG appendixes and workbook. Fluid availability: CWOG Appendix E.

LOUT: FAA 2025–2026, original issue 12 August 2025. Tables 55, 56 and 58, high-speed °C values. All 61 listed Type I products are included.

Airport names, cities and codes: embedded OurAirports public-domain snapshot, 14 September 2026.

Reference season is fixed; no live dataset updates or live weather feed.

Reference limitations

Standard concentrations use FAA LOUT. Other Type I dilution requires a DSP-verified LOUT and actual mixture freezing point; no dilution curve is inferred. Products listed only as supplied have no numerical maximum in the source, so another dilution cannot be validated.

YD-101 and YD-101A are separate products. No standard FAA LOUT is borrowed between them.

Nordwing PG4 has an unresolved “O:04” source cell; that exact combination cannot produce a HOT.

Some station fluid names remain unresolved. Search the approved list and select the actual product.

Published test-expiry annotations remain in the source qualification records. This historical prototype does not establish current fluid qualification.
